title: Can I BEAT War for Throne?
summary: Obscure 4-player variant 'War for Throne' on a chess.com custom 4-player board ringed by stone walls around a central throne. Pawns promote to kings on the 4th rank; those promoted kings fight as ordinary pieces. Only your original (royal) king counts: walking it onto the central throne squares wins. Checking any king 5 times = checkmate. Kings score 3 points, checkmates 40 (transcript also says a 5-check mate is worth 20). He plays 3 FFA games vs humans (1796-1900 rated): wins game 1 by running his king to the middle (collecting 40 x 3 remaining kings = 120 points), 2nd in games 2 and 3.
rules: 4-player free-for-all (Red, Blue, Yellow, Green), chess.com 4PC-style board with stone wall squares ringing a central area.
Placing your own royal king on a centre (throne) square wins the game and collects 40 points for every enemy king still on the board.
Checking any royal king 5 times is equivalent to checkmate (the royal king has 5 'lives').

Pawns promote to kings on the 4th rank (their own relative rank); promoted kings are non-royal and move/capture as normal kings; non-royal kings can stand next to each other and can participate in mating royal kings.
Promoted kings in the centre do nothing - only the royal king wins by reaching the throne.
Scoring: capturing a (promoted) king = 3 points; checkmate = 40 (transcript also quotes 20 for 5-check mate); pawn = 1.
win_condition: First royal king to reach the central throne wins; otherwise highest points when the game ends (checkmates/resignations eliminate players).
